candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand-hygiene auditing / evaluation of staff infection-control practice
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the Hawthorne effect as a limitation of direct observation when interpreting hand-hygiene compliance data.

options.A: Staff may improve hand-hygiene behavior when they know or suspect they are being observed, which can bias the measured rate upward
options.B: Direct observation cannot be used to assess hand-hygiene adherence in health care settings
options.C: Direct observation measures only surgical hand antisepsis and cannot capture routine hand-hygiene opportunities
options.D: Observation completely eliminates sampling and observer-related measurement bias

candidate.rationale: CDC literature on hand-hygiene compliance monitoring identifies the Hawthorne effect as a recognized concern with observation-based measurement: behavior can change in the presence of observation, potentially making observed adherence appear better than usual practice. Direct observation remains an established auditing method, so B and C are incorrect, and observation does not eliminate other sources of measurement bias.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The Hawthorne effect is a recognized limitation/measurement concern when hand-hygiene compliance is assessed through observation.
candidate.source_document_title: Reduction of Healthcare-Associated Infections by Exceeding High Compliance with Hand Hygiene Practices
